A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LSSA/LSSAR research and contain readable text, equations, tables and figures. All material was inspected, including v5 Appendices A–B. v4 ends with references and has no separate appendix.

before.justification: v4 reports original GPT-2 training experiments, attention ablations, length-extrapolation losses, passkey retrieval and downstream benchmark results.

after.justification: v5 retains those empirical results and adds model-scale and training-data comparisons, computational measurements, LAMBADA evaluation and orbital force-prediction experiments.

M1.justification: Equations (4)–(5) retain the same normalized, length-scaled Softplus attention and shifted ReLU-power re-weighting. Algorithm 1 and the log-space formulation explain equivalent computations. Applying LSSAR to additional model sizes and physical prediction tasks does not establish a change to the proposed attention method.

E1.justification: v5 retains v4's language-modeling, retrieval and downstream coverage, while adding filtered educational training data through FineWeb-Edu, LAMBADA last-word prediction, and simulated planetary trajectories with force prediction and symbolic regression. These substantially broaden the represented data and task requirements.

E2.justification: The Softmax, Sigmoid and ReLU comparator set in v4 Table 4 is retained in v5 Table 1. The new physical-law comparison adds an Oracle (KNN) comparator alongside GPT (Softmax) in Table 3. The frontier-LLM results discussed nearby are attributed to Vafa et al., rather than newly evaluated by this work.

E3.justification: New protocols include 45M, 124M and 355M FineWeb-Edu models trained for 9,000, 18,865 and 60,000 steps; a 109M model pretrained on 10M orbital sequences and fine-tuned for force prediction; and symbolic-regression evaluation. Appendix B.2 also introduces a single-A100, batch-4, bfloat16 timing and memory benchmark. The original FineWeb training setup remains otherwise stated as before.

E4.justification: v5 adds attention-sink case studies, model-scale and training-distribution robustness analyses, the LAMBADA collapse analysis, computational-cost analysis and force visualizations across planets. The original sign/centering, Softmax-component, activation-function and re-weighting-parameter ablations are retained in Appendix B.1, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report passkey accuracy averaged over 100 trials with randomly positioned passkeys. v5 applies the same practice to additional model scales and introduces no new training-seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical-testing procedures.

E6.justification: The numerical results in v4 Tables 1–5 are retained in v5 Tables A4–A6 and 1–2. Substantial new results include force-law fits, FineWeb-Edu scaling and retrieval results, LAMBADA scores and computational costs. For example, newly reported 124M FineWeb-Edu LAMBADA accuracies are 8.79% for Softmax and 30.37% for LSSAR; these are additional results, not revisions of v4 scores.

T1.justification: Beyond the retained power-limit argument, v5 adds log-space and temperature derivations, asymptotic gradient calculations in Equations (A6)–(A9), graph-connectivity arguments and FLOP/I/O complexity reasoning. This substantially expands the mathematical analysis, although Algorithm 1 mainly restates the existing method.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion add attention-sink mitigation and physical-world understanding as central claims. A new contribution asserts recovery of Newton's gravitational law, and the conclusion emphasizes a fitted constant closer to the theoretical value than the Oracle baseline. These substantially broaden v4's stability, extrapolation and downstream-performance claims.

C2.justification: v5 substantially revises explanations of retained ablations around gradient coupling and dead neurons, replacing earlier masking-rank and spline arguments. It adds biological, thermodynamic, geometric and causal-filtering interpretations, explanations of training-distribution effects, and implications for reasoning models. Computational overhead is reframed as an engineering artifact with claimed potential for optimized parity.

D1.justification: v5 adds benchmark-specific details including PySR usage, the six-layer 45M configuration, timing precision and batch size, and the attention-map input text and clipping range. It also omits v4's explicit Dynamic NTK Scaling disclosure. This reduces clarity about that retained experimental detail without establishing that the underlying runs changed.

R1.justification: Research positioning expands to distinguish LSSAR from Performer, Longformer, Mamba, Sparsemax and Entmax, and to connect it with biological normalization, world-model discovery and recent reasoning architectures. v4's T6 and Mirage recommendations disappear. These are substantive positioning changes beyond bibliographic updates to retained citations.

P1.justification: v5 extensively rewrites the methodological rationale, introduction, discussion and conclusion, introduces numbered section hierarchies, and moves the original ablations into appendices. It also adds an impact statement and reorganizes the narrative around physical-law discovery alongside length extrapolation.

P2.justification: The opening validation-loss plot is replaced by a three-panel force-prediction figure. Original ablation displays move to the appendix, while new physics and computational tables, multi-scale plots and extensive attention-map grids are added. The title/header layout changes, and the new appendices use a single-column layout.

improvement.justification: Added scale/distribution tests and measured computational costs strengthen v4's limited empirical support. However, v5 elevates physical-world understanding to a central claim partly using comparisons between fine-tuned and cited in-context models, while Appendix A.6's purported full gradient analysis omits the final normalization in Equation (5). These material empirical gains and new weaknesses in claim support leave the net quality direction uncertain.
